leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer B045 with the identical trio Crews, Deshaies and Handa, framed as a concept (PROTACs) plus a mechanism (cereblon and molecular glues). They share the view that induced proximity is a designable, event-driven chemical principle. They differ in wording: Chabes names both bifunctional degraders and glues in the citation, Aili stresses that the citation should state openly that it rewards the concept and cereblon rather than the optimisation work, and the chair's own text speaks of removing disease-relevant proteins. Three further members rank B045 as an alternative (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Sparr), but they do not prefer it in their round-1 configuration and are not counted as supporters here.

Two members prefer Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling for Buchwald and Hartwig as a two-person prize. They share the case of clean attribution, more than 25 years of independent confirmation and broad use in process chemistry. Somfai's citation adds 'a general method for constructing aryl amines' and Zou's is shorter. Both flag the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi/Migita precursor question, and both would keep Kosugi out as a third name, or at least treat that as unresolved (Somfai lists the Kosugi/Migita priority as an open uncertainty). Neither claims a new modality; the case rests on maturity and attribution.

Aqvist alone prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles, for Cullis, Anderson and Langer, on the strength of demonstrated global consequence (siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines) and a pKa-based design principle. He concedes attribution is the weak point and names B045 as first alternative. Other members acknowledge the impact but question what single chemical discovery stands apart from formulation engineering, and Cullis is the only name he and others treat as a defensible core.

Sparr alone prefers biomolecular condensates for Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, valuing a new physical-chemical concept of molecular organisation. She herself concedes that the in vivo picture is contested and that Pappu and Mittag fall outside a three-name cut. Aili and Brzezinski both call the field the least settled of the leading candidacies.

Brzezinski alone prefers long-range electron transfer through proteins for Gray and Winkler, a bounded two-person attribution with a quantitative principle. He discloses that his own field is adjacent and that B006 had first-place support only from him in the openings. The recurring question from others is how it differs from the 1992 Marcus prize and how far its reach extends beyond bioenergetics.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 files name exactly one prize part with a single ballot ID and at most three laureates, and every member lists the criteria they apply: a clear chemical principle, independent confirmation and defensible attribution.

B045 is the only candidate preferred by three members and named as an alternative by three more (six of eight members place it in their first choice or alternatives); no other ballot has more than two explicit supporters.
Every member who discusses B069 accepts that it has the cleanest attribution and the longest record of confirmation on the shortlist; its critics object only on novelty relative to the 2010 prize.
Every member who discusses B009 accepts its demonstrated real-world impact; the disagreement is about attribution and whether it is chemistry rather than medical technology.
No member reports a conflict that would require recusal on any shortlisted candidate.
scientific_disputes: Whether targeted protein degradation is one discovery or two: PROTACs (a designed bifunctional concept, 2001 onward) versus molecular glues and cereblon (a mechanism uncovered for an existing drug). Aili, Brzezinski and Somfai raise this; Chabes and the chair defend a two-strand citation.

Whether C-N coupling (B069) is a distinct achievement with its own ligand-design and mechanistic content, as Somfai and Zou argue, or an extension of the recognised 2010 cross-coupling area, as Chabes, Brzezinski, Sparr and the chair worry.

Whether ionizable lipid delivery (B009) contains a single chemical insight (the pKa-dependent lipid, per Aqvist and Somfai) or is an optimisation of lipid structure and formulation (per Chabes and the chair), and whether it belongs to chemistry or to Physiology or Medicine.

Whether in vivo biomolecular condensates are equilibrium liquid-liquid phase separation at all (Chabes, Aili, Brzezinski) or whether the physical-chemical principle is established enough to cite (Sparr).

Whether B006 is the experimental continuation of Marcus theory (1992) or a new physical principle of tunnelling through the protein medium (Brzezinski raises it himself; the chair, Sparr and Zou's file note that it builds on Marcus theory, while Brzezinski argues the experimental demonstration of tunnelling through protein is the new content).
attribution_disputes: B045: the three-name cut Crews, Deshaies, Handa excludes Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim (first proof of concept) and Ito (cereblon with Handa). Chabes keeps Handa over Ciulli because cereblon is different in kind; the chair lists whether Ciulli displaces or joins Handa as open.

B009: credit is divided between the Vancouver strand (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) and the MIT strand (Anderson, Langer), with patent disputes noted; Aqvist's trio is Cullis, Anderson, Langer and Sparr suggests Cullis, Hope, Madden as an alternative framing. Aqvist concedes the Vancouver priority argument.
B069: Kosugi (tin-amide coupling, on the credited list) and Migita (not on the credited list) as precursors; Somfai and Zou would not add Kosugi as a third laureate.
B008: Pappu and Mittag (sequence grammar) versus Rosen or Brangwynne in a three-person cut.
B006: the tunnelling-pathway picture involves Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton and others, who a Gray and Winkler pairing would leave out.

B026 (an alternative for Aili, Chabes and Somfai): Chabes would name Liu alone while Chabes's file reports that Aili proposes Liu with Komor and Gaudelli, with an unresolved overlap with the Nishida and Kondo cytidine editor.
maturity_disputes: B045: no degrader is approved as a drug at scale, so recognition may rest on trial data and the concept ahead of the clinical verdict (raised by Aqvist, Chabes, Aili, the chair and Somfai). Aili notes the glue branch, thalidomide analogues, is already clinically mature, unlike the PROTAC branch.
B069: maturity is not in dispute; the question is whether a mature, incremental-by-ligand-design method should outrank a newer modality.
B008: the field is still actively debated on definition and in vivo relevance, which several members regard as premature.

B009: demonstrated at global scale, the most mature impact among the leading candidates, but the mRNA vaccine story overlaps with the 2023 Medicine prize according to Chabes, while Aqvist argues it completes rather than repeats that story.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski discloses that his field (biological electron and proton transfer) is close to B006 and B022, and that he is a Stockholm University colleague of Zou; no personal link to any candidate.
Somfai discloses professional closeness, as a synthetic organic chemist, to the B069 field, with no tie to Buchwald or Hartwig.
Zou discloses that B013 touches his own field of electron crystallography, with no tie to the credited names, and notes his Stockholm University colleagueship with Brzezinski.

Aili discloses research overlap with Sparr on self-assembly relevant to B008, not at recusal level; Sparr discloses overlap with B008 and B009 science but no personal or institutional tie to credited persons.
Chabes discloses topical adjacency to B026 and B050 (DNA fidelity, sequencing), not a personal connection.
Linke (chair) notes Lund colleagues Somfai and Sparr and no candidate linked to Lund in his profile.
questions_for_round2: B045: Should the citation be a single concept-plus-mechanism formulation (PROTACs and molecular glues), or should the committee decide that Handa's cereblon work and the Crews/Deshaies PROTAC concept are separable achievements?

B045: Within a three-name cap, does Ciulli displace Handa, does neither change, or does the committee accept that no trio is defensible? What is the committee's explicit reasoning for excluding Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito?

B045 versus B069: Does the committee weigh a new modality that lacks an approved PROTAC drug above a mature method with clean attribution, and what evidence of clinical or practical consequence would members need for B045 to count as mature?
B069: What precisely did C-N coupling add chemically that the 2010 cross-coupling prize did not cover, and does the Kosugi/Migita chronology change who should be credited?

B009: Can Cullis, Anderson and Langer (or any three names) be defended against Hope, Madden and MacLachlan, and does the committee treat ionizable lipid delivery as chemistry given the 2023 Medicine prize?

B008 and B006: What would members need to see settled about in vivo condensates and about the relation to Marcus theory before either becomes a prize candidate, and would any member move from an alternative to a first choice?

Would any member support a two-part prize, such as B045 with B069 or another pairing, given the three-person limit forces a single laureate in the second part, and which pairing would be least arbitrary?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one plurality position, B045 with three explicit supporters and the same trio, against four single or paired preferences (B069 with two, and B009, B008, B006 with one each). The leading debate is between novelty and modality (B045) and maturity and attribution clarity (B069), with B009 posing the strongest impact-versus-attribution trade-off. The record contains no majority of five for any configuration, and each leading position carries a stated weakness from its own proponents. Round 2 should concentrate on credit boundaries, the clinical-maturity threshold for B045, and the novelty relative to prior prizes for B069, B009 and B006.
